errors.what: The dotted inhibin loop ends in a flat bar on the FSH arrow below the anterior pituitary.
errors.why_wrong: Inhibin reduces FSH production and secretion at the anterior pituitary. Placing the bar on the outgoing FSH pathway may suggest that inhibin acts on FSH after its release.
The ovarian axis uses pulsatile GnRH. TRH primarily regulates TSH and prolactin.

errors.what: “ACTH” and “TSH” label the two anterior-pituitary-to-ovary arrows.
errors.why_wrong: The ovarian gonadotropins are LH and FSH. ACTH primarily targets the adrenal cortex, and TSH targets the thyroid.

errors.what: The dotted inhibin feedback ends at the pituitary output labeled “ACTH,” while its text says “FSH only (−).”
errors.why_wrong: The arrow contradicts the label and caption. It should terminate on an output labeled FSH.

errors.what: “LH surge and a smaller FSH surge” sits beside the dashed ovarian feedback arrows, but neither pituitary output shows a surge.
errors.why_wrong: The diagram names the surges without showing increased LH and FSH release toward the ovary, so the causal sequence is incomplete.
